result.journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
result.keywords:
Abstract
Background
Chinese clinical notes contain rich entity-level information and irregular temporal signals that are both useful for downstream prediction tasks. Existing approaches often model these sources separately, which can limit predictive performance and interpretability. This study investigates a hybrid feature representation that combines attention-based sequence encoding with summary statistics extracted from physiological time series.

Methods
We propose a clinical prediction framework that first applies an attention-based CNN-LSTM-CRF module to identify entities in Chinese clinical text, then merges the extracted semantic indicators with a compact set of time series summary statistics. The statistical features include measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape. We evaluate the resulting representations on three common clinical prediction tasks using cross-validation and a feature selection procedure to identify the most informative feature subsets.

Results
Experiments on electronic health record data showed that the combined representation consistently outperformed text-only and statistics-only baselines. Dispersion-oriented measures were especially useful for short-term deterioration and length-of-stay prediction, while central tendency features contributed more strongly to mortality and diagnosis tasks. The hybrid model produced stable improvements across validation folds and yielded several compact feature combinations with competitive performance.

Conclusion
Combining attention-based clinical entity recognition with carefully chosen temporal summary statistics can improve prediction quality while retaining interpretability. The results suggest that hybrid representations may offer a practical direction for future work in Chinese clinical information extraction and downstream patient risk modeling.
